name: Ui_ItemScreen_HandleInput
summary: Input handler for the item screen: forwards the stick direction to the row list, refreshes the highlighted row and, on confirm, checks whether the item can be used/sold and can be afforded, then sets the price/owned message arguments and hands over to the quantity or commit handler.
evidence: Body dispatches on the input-record flags from func_00641F7C (bit 1 = direction -> list vtable +0x3C, bit 8 = row value change, 0x102 = confirm); the confirm chain now runs through named Shop_CanAffordItem, Item_LookupRecord, Message_SetArg and Ui_ItemScreen_CommitSelection. Old name described only the confirm bit.

name: Ui_EquipmentList_HandleInput
summary: Handles the equipment screen's selection input: on the scroll bit it refreshes the highlighted member row and the status-panel character field, on the 0x102 bits it writes the member name into message argument 3 and calls the item-detail pane virtual.
evidence: Read the body: f_1BC bit 1 -> Ui_EquipmentList_GetClampedRow + Item_LookupRecord + Ui_StatusPanel_SetCharacterField; 0x102 -> Message_SetArg(3, member+0xCA) then the f_10D0 virtual +0x10 (open detail). Old name 'Update' hid that the whole body is input dispatch.

name: Ui_EquipmentList_Scroll
signature: void Ui_EquipmentList_Scroll(EquipmentScreen* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Scrolls the equipment list with wrap-around (negative -> last row, past the end -> 0), keeps the two visible columns in sync and refreshes the selected-entry message; pops the pane when the close bit is set.
evidence: Named callees Ui_ScrollList_ScrollToIndex, maybe_Ui_List_IsCursorAtEnd and Ui_EquipmentList_GetClampedRow plus the explicit wrap arithmetic in the body; same f_1BC input flags as the sibling 0x00199A10. No conflicting role found.

name: maybe_Ui_PokerWindow_ConfirmTail
summary: Tail half of the poker confirm logic (0x001E53F8) that Ghidra split out: the frame is lost (self survives only as unaff_r4), so just the shared result code - coin/price lookups, Message_SetArg and the window-stack pops - is readable. A fragment, not a callable API.
evidence: 0x001E53F8 is now confidently named Ui_PokerWindow_Confirm and this body is its second half with stack slots instead of locals and no callers, so 'Dup' described decompiler duplication rather than behaviour. The real entry semantics remain unreadable, hence maybe_ and 0.30.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_SelectSlot
signature: u32 Gfx_Sprite2D_SelectSlot(SpriteActor* self, const void* key, void* entry)
summary: Selects the cached sprite sub-entry for an idle animation: when the scene tick is idle and the scene is not type 0x0F it resolves the key, computes the entry's index in the +0x2A4..+0x3C4 cache and stores it in the draw-selection byte +0x3C8.
evidence: Named caller Actor_TrySelectIdleAnimation consumes the selection when picking the idle animation, matching the cache scan and the +0x3C8 store. The unaff_r7 in the C is only a register the decompiler lost across a call: disassembly 0x001A54E8 loads r8 = [work+0x54->+0x20] and 0x001A5520 reads its f_38 scene type, so the 'idle and scene type != 0xF' guard is verifiable, not damaged semantics.

name: maybe_Ui_JumonWindow_UpdateEntryDescription
summary: Builds the description for one spell/ability entry: when the item byte or spell byte is set it fills message argument 5 from the item/spell description, compares the entry's unlock field with the party member's level and either closes the entry or pushes the description pane with message 0x26.
evidence: Body reads Ui_Message_GetItemDescription / Ui_Message_GetSpellDescription -> Message_SetArg(5), then func_0035EB98(member) + f_16 decides between vtable+8 close and Ui_JumonWindow_PushPane(0x72A390, 0x26). Old name 'ValidateArgs' covered only the limit test, not the description build.

name: Ui_TextArg_NextEntry
summary: Resolves the next text argument: pops one queued argument byte and uses it as an index into the widget's argument table; when the byte queue is empty it converts the pending record into message args 5/8 or applies a 16-byte name record as args 5..7.
evidence: Struct offsets in the body (+8/+0xA/+0xC) match the already-named Ui_Message_SetNameArgs3, and Message_SetArg / Text_FormatMessageArg are named callees; the pop idiom is identical to other named queue helpers. The one Item_LookupRecord call is not an item-table walk: it only serves the branch where the pending argument id is below 0xB3B, formatting the item name into arg 5 and its count into arg 8, while plain numbers and 16-byte name records take the other branches.

name: maybe_Ui_PlateWidget_BindEntry
summary: Binds one bag/medal entry into a plate widget: fetches the plate_base layout, writes the icon/background/text values through the 0x0064xxxx text helpers, maps the plate style (0..5) to a variant and flags the two side icons.
evidence: Named callers are the plate formatting helpers (Ui_Plate_FormatPlayerTitle, Ui_Entry_GetDisplayText, Ui_Plate_GetCharacterFaceId) and the body only writes text elements and icon bits - there is no draw submission, so 'Draw' overstated it.

name: Ui_JumonWindow_Confirm
signature: void Ui_JumonWindow_Confirm(int* self, int arg2, int arg3, int context)
summary: Confirm handler for the small spell/party pane: on the confirm bit it passes the cursor id to the target window's virtual and sets message argument 3, on cancel it starts the close animation.
evidence: Named callees Party_GetMemberIdAtCurrentPage, Ui_StatusPanel_SetCharacter and Ui_Window_PopPaneRaw form the confirm/cancel pair, and the caller set is the jumon window band; nothing contradicts the role.

name: Ui_JumonWindow_UpdatePartyText
signature: void Ui_JumonWindow_UpdatePartyText(JumonPartyText* self, int arg2, int arg3, int context)
summary: Fills one line of the spell window for a party member: looks the member up by index, writes name (record +0xCA) and level into the message arguments with their colours, then advances the entry animation (0x2A/0x2B).
evidence: func_0035EB98 (named party-member record getter) is called with the member index and the already-named Text_ClampRowWidth / Ui_ApplyTextColorAlt handle the text layout; name matches both data source and output.

name: Ui_ShopItemList_HandleInput
signature: void Ui_ShopItemList_HandleInput(UiShopItemList* shop, int screen, int arg3, u8* flags)
summary: Input handler of the shop item list: drives the row cursor and page, toggles the list mode between 1 and 2, refreshes the quantity/price columns and delegates the confirm to the shop entry handler.
evidence: Body calls the named Ui_ItemListCore_InitState, maybe_Party_PlaceItemInMemberSlot, Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry and reads the input flags from func_00641F7C; the 1.6 KB body is a full input state, not a helper.

name: Ui_ShopItemList_MoveCursor
summary: Moves the cursor in the shop item list: page-wraps the row cursor (page size 0xB), updates the visible row and scrollbar and, on confirm, hands over to the price/quantity handler.
evidence: Named callees Ui_List_SelectEntryById, maybe_Ui_ListCursor_IsAtLastRow/IsPastLastRow and Ui_TextScroll_End plus the explicit page arithmetic (magic 0x2AAAAAAB divide, page size 0xB); caller set is the shop screen band.

name: Ui_ItemScreen_SelectQuantity
summary: Quantity selection for the item screen: takes the chosen count from the screen state, clamps it against the owned count, updates the icon count and the price message argument 6, then commits the selection.
evidence: Body reads the screen's f_1E51 count, calls Item_LookupRecord, sets arg 6 from func_0066C99C(record,1) (price) and ends in Ui_ItemScreen_CommitSelection - every step is now a named call.

name: maybe_Ui_PokerWindow_StoreCard
signature: void maybe_Ui_PokerWindow_StoreCard(PokerWindow* self, int cardIdx, int arg3, int context)
summary: Damaged Thumb fragment of the poker window: Ghidra lost the frame (unaff_r4..r8), but the surviving calls store the chosen card id/price into the window state and set message argument 5. Kept maybe_ because the operands are unreadable.
evidence: Re-checked: only Item_LookupRecord, func_0066B41C, Message_SetArg(5) and the 0xA19 item-id range survive; neither the caller (poker confirm path) nor the named callees pin down which card fields are written. No new evidence.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageQueue_Pop
summary: Pops the head of a small message queue: re-formats the entry's three u16 ids through the message formatter, pushes them as message arguments 5..7 and shifts the 0xE0-byte entry block down one slot. Kept maybe_ because the queue owner is inferred from a vtable slot only.
evidence: The shift-from-+0x14-to-+4 loop and Message_SetArg(5..7) are unchanged; no named caller or callee beyond Item_LookupRecord/Text_FormatMessageArg identifies the owning class, so the 'Ui_MessageQueue' prefix stays a guess.

name: Ui_Window_GetMessageArg
summary: Returns this window's message-argument id, building it from the current text token on demand and clearing the cache; for ordinary characters it also registers the character's display name as argument 3.
evidence: Named callee maybe_Ui_Window_BuildMessageArgFromToken and the named Message_SetArg(3, member+0xCA) path match the getter contract (return cached value, clear self+4); the side effect is explained by the UI-band caller.

name: Text_MessageStack_Pop
summary: Pops the last entry of a message stack: if the vector is non-empty it clears the shown message, rebinds arguments 2/3 for the promoted entry, refreshes the shared message view, compacts the 0x2C-byte records and shrinks the vector.
evidence: 0x2C record stride appears in every pointer step, std_memcpy/std_memmove and Message_SetArg are named, and the visible-message refresh uses already-named func_00707C1C; the 'stack pop' interpretation is fully supported.

name: maybe_Ui_MessagePanel_ExecStateA
summary: State handler of the message panel: honouring the pending flags at +0x2048 (bit 2 forces the wait state, bit 0 resets the message object), it looks up the queued message id and emits opcode 3 for unknown ids or opcode 2 with argument 2, pushing the matching pane in both cases.
evidence: Vtable 0x0072A210 and the shared emitter func_003B0F44 are the only anchors; Ghidra dropped two blocks and the opcode values are not tied to any named producer, so 'ExecStateA' cannot be pinned to a specific state.

name: maybe_Ui_Message_SetNameArg
summary: Writes the name of the character stored at self+8 into message argument 2 via the party record (+0xCA), then uses the u16 at +0x0A to pick the argument index for the remaining value; the tail was not decoded (bad instruction data).
evidence: Same Game_GetWork -> func_0035EB98 -> Message_SetArg pair as other named name-argument writers, but two call sites end in halt_baddata, so the second half (the index choice) remains unverified.

name: Ui_PageList_ShowPage
summary: Pages a five-row text list: rewrites the five visible rows from page*5, blanks unused rows, formats the row number into message argument 8 and rebinds the cursor to the page's row count.
evidence: Body loop i<5 over page*5, named Message_SetArg/Ui_List_SelectEntryById and the reciprocal-multiply row count; callers are the already-named Ui_PageList_StepCounterUp/Down, exactly the pager contract.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_FlushAndShowStateMessage
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_FlushAndShowStateMessage(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: Empties the window's pending queue, then shows a state-dependent system message: state 3 uses message 0x11 (and clears argument 8), every other state uses message 0x10 and writes state+1 into the shared message view; finally shows message 0x2E in the sub-pane at +0x1FA8.
evidence: Read the body: nothing supports a 'profile screen' owner (it only reads work+0x2D544 and its own pane), and func_0062F070/func_0010EBD8 are still unnamed, so 'drain the queue' is the earlier pass's reading. The fixed-message sequence is certain, so the prefix was neutralised and maybe_ kept.

name: maybe_Message_SetArgTextPair
summary: Installs one text argument and two label strings into the message-argument store (argument 5 plus the two 0x00707C1C label slots) and clears the 0x40-byte scratch block.
evidence: Only Message_SetArg is named; the two 0x00707C1C calls still take opaque literals, so 'TextPair' describes the call shape rather than the data.

name: Menu_OpenMessageDialog1C
summary: Shows fixed system message 0x1C in the menu: links the owner, selects the message pane at owner+0x118, sets message argument 6 to self+0x750 and formats id 0x1C into the pane.
evidence: Identical five-call sequence to the identified siblings (0x0025A82C id 0x17, 0x0025B704 id 0x1B, 0x0025A7E0 id 0xC), all using Message_SetArg + func_001F0BE4(id) + func_001DAB30(owner+0x118); only the id differs.

name: Menu_OpenMessageDialog0C
summary: Same fixed-message helper as 0x0025A25C but for message id 0xC: links the owner, selects the pane at owner+0x118, sets message argument 6 and formats id 0xC.
evidence: Byte-level sibling of 0x0025A25C (only the id constant differs), and the surrounding 0x0025A8xx / 0x0025B7xx helpers share the idiom, so the family is established.

name: Ui_TextArgWidget_OpenMessage
summary: Shows fixed system message 0x10 in the owner's pane at +0x118: fills message arguments 5 and 6 from the current row record (fields +0x18 and +0x11C) and pushes the message.
evidence: Read the body: same Message_SetArg -> func_001F0BE4(id 0x10) -> func_001DAB30(owner+0x118) idiom as the Menu_OpenMessageDialog family. The old name read the message id 0x10 as a constructor argument count.

name: Ui_Message_SetNumberArg8
summary: Formats a number and installs it as message argument 8: builds text frame self->f_10<<16 plus 2 and icon frame plus 3, with format width 0x14 and the wrap helper on the widget's index table.
evidence: Message_SetArg(8) and the number formatter func_006F0E5C are named, and the body is a pure setter with no counting logic, so 'SetMessageArgCount' was misleading. Frame values distinguish it from 0x00316024.

name: Ui_Message_SetNumberArg8Alt
summary: Second variant of the numeric argument setter: same Message_SetArg(8) and icon wrap, but uses text frames self->f_10<<16 plus 0 / plus 1 and format width 0x32.
evidence: Body is identical to 0x00315F98 apart from the frame numbers and the 0x32 width constant; the same family name with an Alt suffix reflects that only layout ids differ.

name: maybe_Ui_Row_SetMessage
summary: Sets the row's formatted message: writes the row value as message argument 8, measures the resulting text through the widget's index table and pushes it into the row's text pane.
evidence: Named Message_SetArg and the shared text-measure/bind calls match a per-row text setter; nothing distinguishes it from the sibling setters, so the vague 'SetMessage' is kept while the summary now says which value is written.

name: Ui_BaseWindow_Close
signature: void Ui_BaseWindow_Close(UiWindow* self, u32 messageId, int arg3)
summary: Shared close handler for four window classes: sets message arguments 5 and 6, applies the optional message id, runs the class close hook and rebinds the panel pointer.
evidence: Occupies slot 9 of four vtables and calls the named Message_SetArg plus the container unlink helper, from destructor/dispatch callers. Behaviour matches 'close', though the exact message ids come from the caller.

name: Ui_Window_SetStatusText
summary: Writes a description/status string into a sub-pane: sets message argument 5 from the widget field, resolves the text id in the object's +0x30C table and binds it to pane key 0xD.
evidence: Caller is now confidently Ui_ListWidget_SetModeA and the sibling 0x00461ADC is used by SetModeB; both share the +0x30C table, corroborating the description-line role.

name: Ui_Window_SetLabelText
summary: Variant of the status-text setter: records the text id in self->f_30 and writes the resolved string to pane key 0 (the main label) instead of 0xD.
evidence: Same call sequence as 0x00460828 with a different pane key, and its caller is Ui_ListWidget_SetModeB - the pair covers 'label' and 'description' respectively.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SetStateMessageArgs
summary: Pushes the two message arguments a screen shows while visible: argument 5 from the shared text core (lazily built) and argument 2 from the formatted name at self+0xC, for states 0/1/2/4/5/6/8.
evidence: Both Message_SetArg calls and the state switch are clear, but the function is only reachable through a vtable slot and the text core getter is still maybe_, so the 'state message' role is not fully proven.

name: Ui_EquipmentWindow_ConfirmEquipSlot
summary: Confirm handler for the equipment-slot list: resolves the highlighted item, plays anim 0x20 with a message pair when the item is flagged (bit 8), otherwise inserts the item name into the line text and plays anim 0x1E/0x1F.
evidence: Named callees Ui_EquipmentWindow_FindItemIndex / PlayAnim and sibling slot 0x729A88 = Ui_EquipmentWindow_UseSelectedItem place it in the equipment confirm family; the item flag test and Text_InsertLineChar are both in the body.

name: Ui_EquipmentWindow_ConfirmItemList
summary: Confirm handler for the owned-item list of the equipment window: same item-record lookup and line-text insert as the slot handler, but always plays anim 0x1E/0x1F and uses the shared descriptor at 0x729ACC.
evidence: Near-identical body to 0x0019B1A8 without the flag-8 branch, registered at 0x729B1C next to the named Ui_EquipmentWindow_SelectItem; the two confirm targets (slot vs item) are now distinguishable.

name: Ui_EquipmentWindow_NavigateLists
summary: Navigates between the equipment window's lists: moves the cursor across party slots and the item list, plays the corresponding selection animations, updates the message text from the table and scrolls the visible list into view.
evidence: Body uses the named ListCursor_IsAtPartyCountSlot* / PlayAnim / ScrollList_ScrollToIndex / Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextFromTable family; the five slot helpers make the cross-list navigation explicit.

name: maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_OnCharacterChanged
summary: Reacts to a character record change: sets the window's dirty flags, lets the slot-reset helper rebind, marks two manager bytes dirty and clears the old overlay containers so the window rebuilds on its next update.
evidence: Read the body: it never writes the record into the window, it only invalidates caches (dirty flags, Container_NamedMap_Clear, manager bytes +0x6F/+0x7D), so 'BindCharacter' promised more than it does. The named callee Ui_StatusWindow_ResetSlotIfCharacterChanged keeps the status-window owner; the manager fields stay unnamed, hence maybe_.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithTalkData
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithTalkData(UiMessageWindow* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Ends the currently displayed talk: stops the talk-data player, hides the message window through the UI manager and releases the cursor/balloon objects.
evidence: All callees are now named (Field_ExitTalkMode is the only caller; Cutscene_ReleaseMessageAndCamera, Event_OnFieldEnd, Ui_GetCore are callees) and the body is the exact teardown chain for a talk.

name: Gfx_SpriteChain_Update
summary: Updates a chain of billboard sprites hanging between two points: steps along up to three segments with a random angular offset from the engine RNG, draws each segment and extends the chain; for sub-type 1 it also allocates the physics proxy and registers a collision proxy.
evidence: Named Gfx_Scene_DrawSprite / Gfx_CollisionProxy_Create / Gfx_SpriteChain_Node_Ctor and the RNG plus 2*pi constants match, and the only caller is Gfx_SpriteChain_Node_Ctor, tying it to the chain class.

name: FieldParty_Talk_Update
summary: Main update of the field party's talk/social mode: drives member placement and facing, talk states, balloons and speaker/target selection for the conversation.
evidence: 36 callees, all in the named FieldParty_* / party-record family (RegisterMemberModel, SelectFormationSlot, MoveActorTowardTarget, UpdateTalkMemberState), and the only caller is FieldParty_TalkPanel_Reset; the name matches the whole call set.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_ArrangeMembersCircle
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_ArrangeMembersCircle(FieldGimmick* self, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Arranges the party members of a gimmick's actor group on a circle around it: computes each member's angle with acos, places it with Field_ActorGroup_PlaceMember, applies the 'Bt_Nut' effect name and plays the SE.
evidence: The 'Bt_Nut'/'Run' literals and std_Acosf + Field_ActorGroup_PlaceMember are unchanged; no named caller (only the vtable registration) shows what triggers it, so 'ArrangeMembersCircle' remains an interpretation.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_DistributePartEffects
summary: Spreads an effect configuration over the gimmick's parts: loops the part array (+0x6C, count f_8C), computes per-part scale/speed factors and writes the twelve effect parameters +0x24C..+0x278 before switching each part on and playing the SE.
evidence: Ghidra still reports bad-instruction data for the per-branch maths (19 unreachable blocks, unaff registers), so only the loop bound, the parameter block and the sound call are certain.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_LayoutConfiguredParts
summary: Positions the configured parts of a gimmick: for each part it applies the configured offset around the actor, sets the tint through the label object and plays the SE; called only from the config-block applier 0x005E0520.
evidence: The only caller is now identifiable as maybe_Field_Gimmick_ApplyConfigBlock and the loop uses func_00650D34 + func_005E74A0; the 'configured parts' wording still rests on that single caller.

name: Field_Action_MoveInput
summary: Applies the analogue-stick direction to the actor as velocity: reads the move/look sticks, applies the dead zone and speed*dt scaling, adds the result to the actor's velocity and finishes the action update.
evidence: Named Input_ReadMoveStick3D / Input_ReadLookStick3D and the dead-zone constant are in the body; its only caller is the horse-input state, which reads the same stick pair.

name: maybe_Monster_FieldBehaviour_UpdateChase
summary: Monster field-behaviour chase update: advances the monster's physics/steering toward its target and refreshes the model each frame. The readable file has no doc header beyond the address, so the role rests on the callee set.
evidence: Re-checked: callees are only the physics update, VectorSignedToFloat, Powf and the transform helper, with no target or monster accessor that could confirm 'chase'. No new context.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlacePartsAlongArc
summary: Lays the gimmick's parts out along an arc: for every part it takes the local matrix, offsets it from the actor position, places the part and updates its tint/alpha when the label object is set.
evidence: The loop (func_00650D34 / func_00645C54) and the radius constants are unchanged; 'arc' still comes from the constant pattern, not from a named callee.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateVariantLayout
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateVariantLayout(FieldGimmick* self, int arg2, int variant)
summary: Per-variant layout update: the variant (0..5) selects the SE ids and part counts, then repositions and tints the affected parts through the part-placement helpers.
evidence: The switch on the variant and the Sound_PlaySeById ids are clear, but the per-case meaning depends on still-unnamed part helpers.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_SpawnDirectionalEffect
summary: Computes the direction from the actor to the referenced target object, normalises it and spawns the reaction effect at the actor offset by that direction; also configures the UI reaction hook and plays an SE.
evidence: Body subtracts the target position from the actor position, normalises with SQRT and calls the effect spawn helpers; the 'reaction' part is inferred from the UI hook.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_MoveAttachmentTowardTarget
summary: Moves the attachment of the referenced actor toward its target: clears the attachment, computes and normalises the direction to the target fields, applies the step and plays the SE.
evidence: Field_Actor_UpdateAttachment and the position subtraction are clear; the write to f_234 (length * factor) is still an unexplained scale, so the exact motion semantics stay uncertain.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateSlotEffects
summary: Updates the per-slot effects of a gimmick: loops the f_1BC slots at stride 0x14, builds and positions each effect through the 0x005DEBA0.. helpers and applies the shared UI label.
evidence: Stride, loop bound and the helper quartet are unchanged; no named caller or callee identifies what a 'slot' represents.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartsVariantE
summary: Part-update variant E: on state 8 it moves all parts of the actor group by the negated direction, otherwise it updates the attachments and part records and plays the SE.
evidence: The state-8 negated vector and the part helpers are clear, but this is one of five near-identical variants differing only in the helper pair, so the letter suffix is a placeholder.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_LayoutPartsFromAnchor
summary: Places the actor's parts starting from an anchor: hides the anchor panel, stores half the anchor distance in f_20 and lays the parts out from the anchor before playing the SE.
evidence: Ui_GetCore vtable +0x28 (hide) and the f_20 = f_14>>1 store support 'anchor', but the anchor object itself is not named anywhere in the body.

name: Actor_UpdateTrailQuad
summary: Builds/updates the actor's trail quad: computes the two side vertices from the current and previous positions, expands the quad by the width factor and writes the four vertices into the trail object.
evidence: Both callers are now named (maybe_Action_UpdateTrailQuadUnlessFlag, maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateTrailWhenNotPaused) and the body uses the quad-vertex helper plus the 1.41421/1.25 constants, corroborating the trail role independently.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_UpdateMotion
summary: Per-frame movement integrator for a sprite actor: advances the node along its stored direction with damping, recomputes the normalised direction when it changes, stops at the target distance and derives the alpha/offset from the view direction.
evidence: The position/direction fields and the acos/sqrt helpers match the sprite-actor motion family; without a caller the body itself is self-contained and consistent with the neighbouring SpriteActor helpers.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_MoveTowardPoint
summary: Turns a sprite actor toward a target point and advances it, choosing between two rotation states depending on whether the target is in front of or behind the current facing.
evidence: Caller is now confidently maybe_Gfx_Actor_UpdateMotion and both branches end in the same named transform apply; the virtual +0x84 selection is unexplained but the steering role is clear.

name: Battle2DUnit_UpdateTurnToTarget
summary: Turn step for a 2D battle unit: projects the direction, dots it against the stored facing, compares the angle with the 0.3/0.1 cosine thresholds and either snaps the unit into place or keeps moving it toward the formation target.
evidence: Threshold constants, std_Acosf, FieldParty_MoveActorTowardTarget and maybe_FieldParty_CalcFormationPosition are all named and read exactly as described; sibling 0x005A147C continues the same sequence.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateReactionA
summary: State-driven reaction of a gimmick: state 8 plays the SE, state 0x10 pushes the shockwave direction onto the actor, state 0x16 applies the follow-up part action and other states advance the sub-state machine.
evidence: Exact case values 8/0x10/0x16 and the actor-handle lookup are clear, but the reaction type is inferred from those ids alone - no named caller documents the state table.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateReactionB
summary: Second state-driven reaction variant: states 8/0x10 behave like 0x005D9334, state 0x28 rebuilds the UI window descriptor and applies the part action.
evidence: Mirrors 0x005D9334 with an extra state 0x28 branch calling the UI descriptor builder; still only state ids, no external documentation.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartsVariantA
summary: Per-variant part update A: resolves the referenced actor and walks its parts through the 0x005DDAC8/0x5DDBBC/0x5DDC74 helpers, placing each and playing the SE. One of several near-identical variants.
evidence: Handle lookup and the func_00650D34 loop are identical to its siblings; the variants differ only in helper addresses, so the A/B/C/D/E letters are ordering labels, not semantics.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartsVariantB
summary: Per-variant part update B: same handle lookup and part loop as 0x005DDA54, using the 0x005DDDC4/0x5DDEB8 helpers (the variant that also updates part tint).
evidence: Same skeleton as 0x005DDA54 with a different helper pair; 'also updates tint' is inferred from the helper call, not verified.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartsVariantC
summary: Per-variant part update C: on state 0x10 it moves all parts by the negated direction vector, then applies the 0x005DDFA8/0x5DE168/0x5DE26C helpers per part and plays the SE.
evidence: The state test and negated vector are readable; the per-part helper meaning is still unknown.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartsVariantD
summary: Per-variant part update D: resolves the referenced actor and walks its parts with the 0x005E144C/0x5E1540 helpers, placing each and playing the SE; same skeleton as 0x005DDA54.
evidence: Only the helper addresses differ from the other variants; no additional context was found.

name: maybe_BattleScene_UpdateUnitKeyframesB
summary: Second keyframe/transform update pass for battle units: initialises four animation tracks (scene+0x308+i*0x3C) and walks the four unit lists applying the alternate timing constants.
evidence: Sole caller is the named BattleScene state dispatcher 0x00606234, and func_0043DC1C is now maybe_Anim_TimeTrack_Init; 'keyframes' still rests on that maybe_ callee.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneSprite2D_InitAnimSlots
